Article Title: 'Distressing': BJP slams Congress over three of its CMs 'skipping' Brics dinner
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party on Tuesday slammed Congress after three of its chief ministers skipped the dinner for Brics leaders hosted by the government, accusing them of "prioritising partisan politics over the national interest. "At a press conference, BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj asked Congress whether, in opposing Prime Minister Narendra Modi, it had begun opposing India as well."Political and ideological differences can always exist in politics. But when it comes to India and national interest, there should be no room for personal animosity or discord," Bansuri said."It is distressing that when the three chief ministers from the Congress party were invited to the Brics summit dinner, they prioritised partisan politics over the national interest .... I would like to ask Congress - in your opposition to PM Modi, have you now started to oppose India as well?" she added.BJP MP's remarks came after official sources said that CMs hailing from opposition parties were also invited for Brics dinner but did not attend the event.While Tamil Nadu CM Vijay was abroad, three Congress CMs invited for the dinner chose to skip it.A day before the dinner on September 12, Telangana CM Revanth Reddy had accepted the invitation for the dinner hosted by PM Modi.However, Reddy's office later conveyed to govt that he would be unable to attend due to "unavoidable circumstances".Two other Congress chief ministers, V D Satheesan of Kerala and D K Shivakumar of Karnataka, also skipped the dinner.The decision to invite CMs of different states for the dinner for BRICS leaders was in keeping with govt's move to host numerous events related to the grouping during India's presidency across various cities, and the decision of opposition CMs to skip it was unfortunate, the sources said.
Article Summary: BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj asked Congress whether, in opposing Prime Minister Narendra Modi, it had begun opposing India as well. While Tamil Nadu CM Vijay was abroad, three Congress CMs invited for the dinner chose to skip it.

Article Title: West Bengal: BJP fields slain Suvendu Adhikari aide's mother for Nandigram bypoll
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party on Tuesday fielded Hansirani Rath, mother of CM Suvendu Adhikari’s late personal assistant Chandranath Rath, from the Nandigram assembly seat for the bypoll.Chandranath was shot dead in West Bengal's Madhyamgram two days before Suvendu took oath as chief minister.Suvendu visited the family shortly after, assuring them he would act as their household guardian.Meanwhile, Hansirani is also a five-term panchayat and panchayat samiti poll winner.The Nandigram seat in Purba Medinipur district was vacated by Adhikari, who retained Bhabanipur after winning both constituencies in the assembly elections. BJP also nominated Sarkar from the Rejinagar assembly constituency for the October 6 bypolls. Sarkar is a former BJP president of Murshidabad district and a member of the party's state committee.The Rejinagar assembly constituency in Murshidabad district was vacated by Aam Janata Unnayan Party founder Humayun Kabir, who had also won from Nowda.On Sunday, the Trinamool Congress announced Sanchita Pradhan (Dey) as its candidate for Nandigram and Rabiul Alam Chowdhury for Rejinagar in the upcoming by-elections.The party made the announcement in a post on X, saying the candidates were being announced under the guidance and inspiration of its chairperson and former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee."All India Trinamool Congress, under the guidance and inspiration of our Hon’ble Chairperson Smt @MamataOfficial, is pleased to announce the candidates for the upcoming Nandigram & Rejinagar by-elections. We wish Smt Sanchita Pradhan (Dey) and Shri Rabiul Alam Chowdhury the very best for this journey. May they carry forward the hopes and aspirations of the people with strength and determination," the party said in the post.From Congress, Mohd. Abdullahil Kafi will contest from Rejinagar assembly constituency, while Milan Pradhan has been named the candidate from Nandigram.
Article Summary: Hansirani Rath, mother of CM Suvendu Adhikari’s late personal assistant Chandranath Rath, is fielded. Rath is also a five-term panchayat and pan chayat samiti poll winner. Nandigram seat in Purba Medinipur district was vacated by Adhkikari.

Article Title: '3 Cong CMs invited to Brics dinner but they didn't turn up'
Article Text:

Article Title: 'Someone from that ward voted for me': BJP candidate gets 1 vote in Rajasthan local body polls
Article Text:
BJP candidate says his vote was in another ward

NEW DELHI: BJP candidate Kailashchand in Rajasthan's urban local body elections found himself at the centre of attention after the results declared that he had received only one vote from the ward that he contested.Kailashchand contested from Ward 13 of the Parbatsar municipality in Didwana-Kuchaman district.According to the state election commission website, Congress candidate Hina Khanam won the ward with 376 votes, while Independent candidate Rashid Khan finished second with 195 votes.Kailashchand told news agency PTI that he was a voter in Ward 12, but the BJP fielded him from the neighbouring Ward 13."I got one vote. My vote is in Ward 12. I was fielded from Ward 13. Someone from that ward has voted for me," he said.The Parbatsar municipality has 25 wards, of which Congress won 13 and the BJP 12.Kailashchand's one-vote tally stood out as counting continued for 309 urban local bodies across Rajasthan.Rajasthan's urban local body election results threw up some strikingly low vote tallies, with a BJP and a Congress candidate securing just one vote each, while a Rashtriya Loktantrik Party (RLP) candidate drew a blank.The results came as counting was under way for elections to 309 urban local bodies across the state.More than 10,000 councillor posts were at stake in the elections.
Article Summary: Rajasthan's urban local body election results throw up some strikingly low vote tallies. A BJP and a Congress candidate secured just one vote each, while a Rashtriya Loktantrik Party (RLP) candidate drew a blank.

Article Title: Cong rejects proposal from Didi's party for bypoll pact
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: An attempt by the Mamata Banerjee faction of TMC to hammer out an alliance with Congress for upcoming bypolls in Bengal did not materialise after the latter insisted on going it alone, reports Subodh Ghildiyal.Trinamool's decision to announce candidates in Nandigram and Rejinagar Monday came well after Congress had named its nominees.But it is learnt that TMC had reached out to Congress with an offer for coordination in the bypolls. The offer was that Congress should contest Nandigram while Trinamool would contest in Rejinagar.However, sources said, the West Bengal congress did not agree to go to the polls with TMC. The argument was that the party is finally looking at renewing its base after complete decimation over last one decade, and a tie-up now would again neutralise the process of reviving the organisation. “Its a local party decision,” sources said, when asked about the absence of alliance between congress and TMC despite the aggression being shown by the bjp, which recently came to power in the Trinamool Fort.A senior leader said there is complete coordination between TMC and congress, and the latter is firmly with the Mamata banerjee outfit when it comes to taking on the bjp over misuse of state power against the rival, adding that the partnership is also evident in the Parliament.“but these are by elections, it is a very local affair. The local unit takes such decisions,” he added.The absence of coordination in Bengal seems to be the reason that Trinamool has also fielded a candidate in the Lok Sabha byelection for Nagaon constituency in Assam. While congress is in a direct fight with Bjp that recently stormed back to power with a massive tally in Assam, TMC staking a claim in the contest threatens to make it a triangular fight. Interestingly, it has fielded a Muslim candidate, which can damage the prospects of the “secular ally”.
Article Summary: Trinamool's decision to announce candidates in Nandigram and Rejinagar Monday came well after Congress had named its nominees. It is learnt that TMC had reached out to Congress with an offer for coordination in the bypolls.

Article Title: How Assam man who vowed to kill wife’s ‘sugar daddy’ ended up dying himself
Article Text:
Ramanuj was supposed to be produced before a court on Monday as his seven days of police custody ended.





GUWAHATI: Ramanuj Goswami, a cab driver accused of murdering his wife, died after allegedly jumping from a moving police vehicle in Guwahati early on Monday, police said.Ramanuj (28) was being taken to Gauhati Medical College and Hospital (GMCH) when the incident occurred near the Nursing College on Narakasur Hill.Goswami was accused of beheading his wife, Riya Talukdar Goswami (25), at their Basisthapur flat on Sept 3. He surrendered on Sept 6. Police recovered her severed head, wrapped in a polythene bag, from a refrigerator and her body from the flat.DCP Tabu Ram Pegu said Goswami complained of feeling unwell and was being taken for a medical examination around 2 am. The police vehicle suffered a puncture near the TV tower, and a tyre had to be replaced.After the journey resumed, Goswami allegedly kicked the constable holding his handcuffs and jumped from the moving vehicle near the Nursing College, Pegu said. He reportedly fell on the road and then jumped towards a roadside slope, sustaining serious injuries. The constable was also injured.“He was immediately taken to GMCH, where he was examined, but the doctor declared him dead,” Pegu said.GMCH superintendent Devajit Choudhury said Goswami was brought to the hospital around 3 am as a road accident case.“The patient was admitted with head injuries and bleeding. He was brought dead to the hospital. Autopsy of the deceased is underway. The causes of death will be ascertained after that,” he said.Goswami’s family in Gauripur, Dhubri district, was informed. His father, Tarun Kumar Goswami, said the family learnt of his death while performing Riya’s shraddha. He initially refused to accept the body but later said he would perform the last rites in Gauripur.
Article Summary: Ramanuj Goswami, 28, was being taken to Gauhati Medical College and Hospital. He was accused of beheading his wife, Riya Talukdar GoswAMI (25), at their Basisthapur flat on Sept 3. Police recovered her severed head from a refrigerator and her body from the flat.

Article Title: Haryana Congress chief slams BJP over Adampur temple demolition, seeks probe
Article Text:
Haryana Congress president Rao Narendra Singh criticized the BJP government's actions.





CHANDIGARH: Haryana Congress president Rao Narendra Singh on Monday accused the BJP government of “double standards” on religion, alleging that bulldozers were being used against centres of faith even as the party sought votes in the name of temples.Reacting to the demolition of the Baba Balaknath temple, gaushala, samadhi site and other religious structures at Adampur Jharsha village in Gurugram’s Sector 50, Rao demanded Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini’s immediate intervention and an impartial probe.Rao alleged that the religious complex had been a centre of worship and cow service for decades and that the land had been given by the village panchayat for the Baba Balaknath Ashram. He said the administration, backed by heavy police deployment, carried out the demolition over nearly 16 hours, removing idols and shifting around 35 cows from the gaushala. He noted that the Shiva temple at the site was left intact.“The government says notices were issued as the land was government property. But why was the issue not resolved through dialogue and with due respect for religious sentiments?” Rao asked.He also demanded an inquiry into villagers’ allegations that the action could benefit builders or the land mafia.Targeting the BJP nationally, Rao cited allegations relating to religious projects at Ayodhya, Kedarnath and Mahakal, claiming the government had failed to act decisively on such issues.Rao said Congress did not use religion as a political weapon and respected all faiths. He demanded reconstruction of the Baba Balaknath temple complex and action against officials found responsible.“On one hand BJP seeks votes in the name of temples; on the other, bulldozers are being used on centres of faith,” he said.
Article Summary: Haryana Congress president Rao Narendra Singh criticized the BJP government's actions. He demanded Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini’s immediate intervention and an impartial probe. Rao alleged that the religious complex had been a centre of worship and cow service for decades.

Article Title: Tamil Nadu shop owner arrested over banner showing Lord Ganesha eating biryani
Article Text:
Based on the complaint, the Tirunelveli city police commenced an inquiry and arrested Jeyanth





MADURAI: Tirunelveli city police on Saturday arrested a biryani shop owner on allegations that a banner depicted Lord Ganesha eating biryani.According to the complainant, Selvaraj, 42, of Narasinganallur, alleged that he had noticed that the banner outside the ‘Dindigul Kalyana Biryani’ shop showed Lord Ganesha eating biryani.He also alleged that the banner was put up with an intention to insult the religious sentiments of Hindus.Based on the complaint, Tirunelveli city police began an inquiry and arrested Jeyanth, 30, of KTC Nagar.He was arrested under Section 299 of the BNS for allegedly committing deliberate and malicious acts intended to outrage religious feelings.
Article Summary: Tirunelveli city police arrested Jeyanth, 30, of KTC Nagar. He was arrested under Section 299 of the BNS for allegedly committing deliberate and malicious acts intended to outrage religious feelings. Selvaraj, 42, of Narasinganallur, alleged that the banner outside the ‘Dindigul Kalyana Biryani’ shop showed Lord Ganesha eating biryani.

Article Title: Quack doctor detained in Maharashtra for practising medicine without registration
Article Text:
A 27-year-old quack doctor was detained by Panvel police after an inspection (Representative image)





NAVI MUMBAI: A 27-year-old quack doctor was detained by Panvel taluka police after a complaint was lodged by the medical officer of the Primary Health Centre at Ajivali village in Panvel taluka, following an inspection by health department officials at his illegal clinic in Kasalkhand village on Monday afternoon.The accused was identified as Noorul Huda Imamul Haq, who hails from West Bengal and resides in an MHADA building in India Bulls Township, Kon village, Panvel.Gajanan Ghadge, senior inspector of Panvel taluka police, informed that the complaint was lodged by medical officer Dr Sayali Mankar, 33, who inspected Haq's clinic in Kasalkhand village and found that he was an unqualified and unregistered medical practitioner allegedly practising modern medicine by posing as a doctor.He had been running the clinic and treating patients for the past one month, police said. The police seized medicines stocked at the clinic as evidence.Inspector Ghadge said, "We have invoked relevant sections of the Maharashtra Medical Practitioners Act, 1961, against the accused, which prohibit any person from practising medicine in the state unless their name is registered under the relevant statutory provisions and prescribe criminal penalties and fines for those who illegally practise medicine without valid registration. Under the law, the accused was served a notice under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), directing him to appear for inquiry when summoned and during the court proceedings. "
Article Summary: The accused was identified as Noorul Huda Imamul Haq, who hails from West Bengal. He had been running the clinic and treating patients for the past one month, police said. The police seized medicines stocked at the clinic as evidence.

Article Title: 'Grabbed hand and attempted to disrobe': Cab driver tries to assault woman passenger near Navi Mumbai airport
Article Text:
Police have registered a case and are searching for the accused driver (Representative image)





NAVI MUMBAI: A woman passenger travelling home after attending a party in Chembur allegedly faced molestation and an attempted assault by a cab driver who took the vehicle to a deserted road near Navi Mumbai airport late on Saturday night, police said on Sunday.The incident took place around 1.30am on the airport service road, about two kilometres from Navi Mumbai airport, police said. The accused allegedly stopped the cab on the pretext of drinking water before moving to the rear seat beside the woman, police said.According to the police, the woman was travelling to Panvel after a friend booked a cab for her following the party."The driver stopped the vehicle on the deserted service road, stepped out briefly, and then re-entered the car, sitting on the rear seat next to the woman. He allegedly grabbed her hand and attempted to disrobe her," said an official of the Navi Mumbai Police.The woman managed to break free and escape from the vehicle, following which the driver allegedly fled the spot.After the incident, the woman contacted her family and went to Panvel Police Station to lodge a complaint.Since the alleged incident took place within the jurisdiction of Navi Mumbai airport police station, Panvel police escorted her to the appropriate police station.Based on her complaint, Navi Mumbai Airport Police registered a case against the accused, identified as Mohammad Afzal Shaikh, under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).Police have launched a search for Shaikh and are using technical intelligence to trace his whereabouts.Further investigation is underway.(With ANI inputs)(The victim's identity has not been revealed to protect her privacy as per Supreme court directives on cases related to sexual assault)
Article Summary: A woman passenger travelling home after attending a party in Chembur allegedly faced molestation and an attempted assault by a cab driver. The incident took place around 1.30am on the airport service road, about two kilometres from Navi Mumbai airport. The woman managed to break free and escape from the vehicle, following which the driver allegedly fled the spot.

Article Title: FIR lodged after 3,400 SIR forms found in Navi Mumbai shop; 5 BLOs suspended
Article Text:
An FIR was registered against Suraj Patil for illegally possessing voter enumeration forms





NAVI MUMBAI: The police have registered an FIR against Suraj Patil, a nodal BJP youth wing committee member, for illegally possessing and converting special intensive revision (SIR) voter enumeration forms for “personal use” and for breaking the maintenance of secrecy of voting under Section 314 of the BNS and Section 128 of the Representation of People Act.Section 314 of the BNS deals with dishonestly converting a movable property for own use, for which the punishment is at least two years imprisonment.The matter came to light on Thursday, after an advocate working for the Shiv Sena (UBT) noticed hundreds of original SIR forms lying at a photocopier’s shop in Kharghar. He alerted the police.The accused (Patil) had decamped from the Kharghar police station, leading to high drama throughout the night.Authorities seized 3,404 SIR forms, including 11 blank ones, of 11 polling stations from the photocopier’s shop next to the Ramsheth Thakur Public School in Sector 19, Kharghar, by Shiv Sena (UBT) nodal chief Balesh Bhojane.Five booth-level officers (BLOs) served with show-cause notices were suspended by the Panvel City Municipal Corporation (PCMC) chief Mangesh Chitale.They include three data entry operators working as booth-level officers from a private company, Saunik Integrated & Security Pvt Ltd, Bhayandar, engaged by the PCMC.Their names are Sulochana Mane, Prashant Mhatre and Rahul Bhagat.The Shiv Sena (UBT) had earlier warned the Panvel sub-divisional officer through a letter about various lapses in the electoral process.A two-member inquiry committee comprising a Panvel deputy municipal commissioner, Nanasaheb Kamathe, and an assistant electoral registration officer, has been formed to conduct a comprehensive probe.Bhojane said, “MLAs Jitendra Awhad and Rohit Pawar have tweeted the video regarding the original SIR forms at the Kharghar shop. We demand action against the Panvel SDO as he did not take preventive measures despite our complaint about forms filed at the BJP offices. The FIR was filed only after more than hundreds of our workers assembled at the police station.”After learning about the incident, Raigad district communication head of Shiv Sena (UBT) Prasad Bhoir lodged a complaint with the electoral registration officer.“Yesterday evening, the election registration office (ERO) received information that a person is xeroxing enumeration forms at a Xerox centre at Kharghar sector 19. Immediately, the assistant election registration officer visited the site and found that one Suraj Patil was holding around 3,400 enumeration forms and xeroxing it illegally,” Raigad district collector Kishan Javale said.
Article Summary: Police have registered an FIR against Suraj Patil, a nodal BJP youth wing committee member, for illegally possessing and converting voter enumeration forms. The matter came to light on Thursday, after an advocate working for the Shiv Sena (UBT) noticed hundreds of original SIR forms lying at a photocopier’s shop in Kharghar.

Article Title: Palghar hospital assault case: MLA Rajendra Gavit's son, 9 Govindas arrested
Article Text:
The accused were produced before the Palghar sessions court, which remanded them in police custody till September 13.





PALGHAR: Palghar police on Friday arrested Rohit Gavit, son of MLA Rajendra Gavit, in connection with the assault and ruckus at Relief Hospital in Palghar.9 other Govindas were also arrested in the case. The accused were produced before the Palghar sessions court, which remanded them in police custody till September 13.The incident took place in the early hours of Saturday, September 5, during the Dahi Handi celebrations, when local Shiv Sena functionaries allegedly created a ruckus at Relief Hospital over the treatment of injured Govindas.They allegedly assaulted a hospital employee and took away five injured Govindas who were admitted to the ICU.Palghar police had registered a case against 17 people, including Shiv Sena district chief Kundan Sankhe and city chief Rahul Gharat.So far, only Gharat had been arrested, while the other accused were absconding. Police had launched a search for them.On Friday, police arrested Rohit Gavit from his residence in Mira Road. According to police, Gavit had obtained a new SIM card and inserted it into his old mobile phone.This helped police trace his location through technical surveillance and arrest him.Police also arrested nine other accused who were among the Govindas involved in the case. They were produced before the Palghar sessions court, which remanded all the accused in police custody till September 13.
Article Summary: Palghar police on Friday arrested Rohit Gavit, son of an MLA, in connection with the assault and ruckus at Relief Hospital in Palghar. The incident took place in the early hours of Saturday, September 5, during the Dahi Handi celebrations. Police had registered a case against 17 people, including Shiv Sena chief Kundan Sankhe and Rahul Gharat.

Article Title: Cases registered against 3 vehicle owners by Pimpri Chinchwad police for illegally using MLA stickers
Article Text:
Representative image

Pune:





Three car owners with stickers reading “Maharashtra Vidhansabha Sadasya, Amdar (MLA)” on their cars were booked by Pimpri Chinchwad police.Cases were registered with Pimpri, Bhosari and Hinjewadi police on Sunday and Monday. The accused have been booked under Section 205 (wearing garb or carrying a token used by a public servant with fraudulent intent) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and relevant sections of the Motor Vehicles Act Police investigations revealed none of the car owners were associated with any MLA in the district. The drivers and owners were questioned about the stickers. “During the inquiry, some drivers told the police that they had put up the stickers with the intention of gaining financial benefits and receiving preferential treatment for their vehicles,” an officer from Pimpri Chinchwad crime branch said. He added, “A search is on for the suspects who made and sold these stickers to car owners. ”
Article Summary: Cases were registered with Pimpri, Bhosari and Hinjewadi police on Sunday and Monday. Police investigations revealed none of the car owners were associated with any MLA in the district. Some drivers told the police they had put up the stickers with the intention of gaining financial benefits and receiving preferential treatment for their vehicles.

Article Title: Pimpri Chinchwad cops seize gutka, flavoured tobacco worth Rs56 lakh
Article Text:
Pimpri Chinchwad police seize gutka, flavoured tobacco

Pune:





Pimpri Chinchwad police recovered gutka and flavoured tobacco worth Rs56 lakh from a truck on the Pune-Mumbai highway on Sunday. The gutka and tobacco sacks were being transported to Mumbai after being hidden under vermicompost. A case was registered with Shirgaon police.Senior police inspector Devendra Chavan of Shirgaon police said his team noticed a truck near the Urse toll plaza during patrolling. “We found the driver’s movements suspicious. We stopped the truck and asked about its contents. He claimed that he was transporting vermicompost to Mumbai,” Chavan said.He said that the team checked the truck and found gutka and flavoured tobacco hidden under the boxes of vermicompost. “We seized gutka worth Rs42.44 lakh, flavoured tobacco worth Rs14.40 lakh, vermicompost worth Rs2.6 lakh and the truck worth Rs20 lakh. We have arrested the truck driver, who is from Bengaluru in Karnataka. We have sent teams to trace the other accused,” he said.
Article Summary: Gutka and tobacco sacks were being transported to Mumbai after being hidden under vermicompost. A case was registered with Shirgaon police. The truck driver, who is from Bengaluru in Karnataka, has been arrested, police said.

Article Title: Six arrested for murdering fellow guest worker in Coimbatore
Article Text:
Coimbatore:





Six guest workers were arrested on Wednesday, in connection with the murder of a fellow guest worker near Othakkalmandapam in Coimbatore district on Monday.Chettipalayam police have identified the arrested as Tuithe Reang, 22, Sunil Rai Reang, 24, Kotho Ram Reang, 30, Sumit Kumar, 20, Sramit Trang, 35, and Santhosh Kumar, 20, all from Tripura.The crime came to light on Tuesday, when an unidentified man’s body was found buried in a pit near Othakkalmandapam within Chettipalayam police station limits. A case was registered and the deceased was eventually identified as Badal Shit, 24, from West Bengal.Investigation revealed that the deceased and the accused were working as housekeeping staff in a private college near Othakkalmandapam. On Monday night they had all consumed alcohol together, and an altercation broke out when the accused asked Badal Shit for money to buy more alcohol, and he refused.“During the altercation, the accused beat him, and Badal Shit died of the severe injuries he suffered in the assault. They then buried him and fled,” said an officer.All six were produced before the judicial magistrate and remanded in custody.
Article Summary: Six guest workers were arrested in connection with the murder of a fellow guest worker near Othakkalmandapam in Coimbatore district. The crime came to light on Tuesday, when an unidentified man’s body was found buried in a pit. A case was registered and the deceased was eventually identified as Badal Shit, 24, from West Bengal.

Article Title: Dharapuram bypoll: ‘Election King’ K Padmarajan first to file nomination
Article Text:
K Padmarajan filling his nomination





TIRUPUR: Filing of nominations for the Dharapuram reserved (scheduled caste) assembly bypoll in Tirupur district began at 11am on Wednesday, with self-styled “Election King” K Padmarajan becoming the first candidate to submit papers before revenue divisional officer A Felix Raja. He is contesting as an independent candidatePadmarajan, a tyre shop owner from Attur in Salem district, said this was his 256th nomination since 1988, filed in Tamil Nadu and other states to underline that ordinary citizens could also contest elections. He claimed that the effort was also part of a Guinness record attempt, adding that he had previously contested against leaders including Prime Minister Narendra Modi, former chief ministers J Jayalalithaa, M Karunanidhi and MK Stalin, and chief minister C Joseph Vijay. He had spent lakhs of rupees on filing nominations over the years.According to the election schedule, nominations can be filed till Sept 16. Scrutiny will be held on Sept 17, and the last date for withdrawal is Sept 19. Polling is slated for Oct 6, and counting will be held on Oct 9.The Dharapuram constituency has been a reserved seat since 1967. The constituency has seen shifting electoral outcomes in recent cycles, with AIADMK winning in 2011, Congress in 2016 and DMK in 2021, before the seat returned to AIADMK in the last assembly election.It is for the first time that a bypoll is going to be held in Tirupur district, which was formed in 2009. The bypoll has been necessitated by the resignation of R Sathyabama, who was the sitting MLA. Sathyabhama, who contested on behalf of AIADMK, won the election from Dharapuram constituency by securing 81,100 votes. She voted in support of the TVK during the floor test in the assembly and subsequently resigned from her MLA post and joined the TVK.Meanwhile, DMK on Wednesday announced S Suganya,33, a lawyer and party women’s wing functionary, as its candidate in the constituency.
Article Summary: Self-styled ‘Election King’ K Padmarajan became the first candidate to submit papers. He said this was his 256th nomination since 1988. Polling is slated for Oct 6, and counting will be held on Oct 9.

Article Title: Solomon Pappaiah Cremated With State Honours
Article Text:
Renowned Tamil scholar and pattimandram moderator solomon pappaiah cremated with state honours





Madurai: Renowned Tamil scholar and pattimandram moderator Solomon Pappaiah, who died in Madurai on Friday, was cremated with full state honours at Thathaneri crematorium on Saturday.Ministers C T R Nirmal Kumar and P Viswanathan, district collector Nishanth Krishna, city police commissioner S Rajendran, and MLA Madhar Badhurudeen paid their last respects to Pappaiah at the crematorium. They laid floral wreaths on behalf of the Tamil Nadu govt. Several officials, political leaders, and members of the public also gathered to pay their respects.Pappaiah, 90, was undergoing treatment for age-related illnesses when his health deteriorated and he died at a private hospital on Friday. Meanwhile, acting mayor of Madurai corporation T Nagarajan announced on Saturday that the corporation will name the street where Solomon Pappaiah lived after him. A resolution will be passed at the council meeting in this regard.
Article Summary: Pappaiah, 90, was undergoing treatment for age-related illnesses when his health deteriorated and he died at a private hospital on Friday. Acting mayor of Madurai corporation T Nagarajan announced on Saturday that the corporation will name the street where Solomon Pappaiah lived after him.

Article Title: Employee held, former principal of American college booked in job scam case
Article Text:
An employee of the American College in Madurai has been arrested in connection with cheating a man of Rs 16 lakh by assuring a job for his daughter in the college.





Madurai: An employee of the American College in Madurai has been arrested in connection with cheating a man of Rs 16 lakh by assuring a job for his daughter in the college.Based on a complaint from M Soman of Karaikudi, police registered a case against Kalaiselvi, her husband Vijayakumar , who is a temporary employee of the college, former principal (retired) M Davamani Christober and guest lecturer Daniel. Police arrested Kalaiselvi on Thursday.According to police, Soman approached Daniel after coming across an advertisement about recruitment of an assistant professor in the college. Thereafter, Daniel introduced Soman to Kalaiselvi and Vijayakumar, allegedly claiming that they were close to the former principal. They sought Rs 45 lakh from Soman for the job. Soman paid Rs 15.75 lakh to them in various instalments in 2024. However, no job was arranged for his daughter.It may be recalled that in Aug, Anna Nagar police registered a case against four people, including former principal Davamani Christober, for cheating a man of Rs 24 lakh by promising a job in the college.
Article Summary: An employee of the American College in Madurai has been arrested in connection with cheating a man of Rs 16 lakh by assuring a job for his daughter in the college. Police arrested Kalaiselvi, her husband Vijayakumar, former principal (retired) M Davamani Christober and guest lecturer Daniel.

Article Title: Instructions issued to regulate queue for senior citizen in Tiruchendur temple, authorities tell HC
Article Text:
The court disposed of the plea after taking into account that necessary instructions were issued to regulate the queue.





Madurai: Madras high court on Monday disposed of a plea seeking a direction to the authorities to prevent irregularities in senior citizens queue for darshan in Subramanya Swamy Temple in Tiruchendur in Thoothukudi district. The court disposed of the plea after taking into account that necessary instructions were issued to regulate the queue.A division bench of Justice C V Karthikeyan and Justice R Sakthivel was hearing a public interest litigation filed by M Seetharaman. The petitioner stated that under the guise of helping senior citizens, several others accompany them to get free darshan, thereby delaying regular devotees in worshipping the deity and causing much hardship.During the course of hearing, authorities submitted that a board was erected regarding the directions issued by the executive officer/joint commissioner of the temple for darshan by senior citizens. The officer had provided instructions about the protocol in place for darshan by senior citizens at 7am and 6pm. Further, chronic patients aged between 60 and 69 years have a separate queue.Those above 70 years can have darshan along with one helper.Necessary instructions were also given on the protocol to be followed by the caretaker. Further instructions were given for pregnant women and those who suffer from physical disabilities, the authorities stated.The bench observed that it is seen that at successive intervals, courts have been issuing directions with respect to the manner in which darshan should be provided for the devotees who visit the temple. “We are confident that necessary steps would be taken and the grievance of the petitioner will be addressed. No further directions are required,” the judges observed and disposed of the petition.
Article Summary: The court disposed of the plea after taking into account that necessary instructions were issued to regulate the queue. The petitioner stated that under the guise of helping senior citizens, several others accompany them to get free darshan. The court observed that it is seen that at successive intervals, courts have been issuing directions.

Article Title: Cyberattacks: Kerala HC directs police protection to TV journalist
Article Text:
Kochi

:





The high court on Monday issued a directive to the police to provide adequate protection to Aparna Kurup, coordinating editor of Big TV, a Malayalam news channel.A bench of Justice Bechu Kurian Thomas issued the directive in a petition filed by Kurup seeking police protection on account of continuous cyberattacks against her on various social media platforms. Kurup alleged in her petition that she had faced severe cyberbullying and threats following a programme aired on the channel criticising the remarks made by Samastha Kerala Jamiyyathul Ulama (A P faction) general secretary Kanthapuram A P Aboobacker Musliyar, concerning Muslim women’s participation in public life, prompting her to approach the HC. It was also stated in the petition that a case was registered on her complaint against the cyberattacks by the Kochi city cybercrime police on Sept 7. She further claimed that she was facing massive online harassment, doxxing and death threats, with fake social media handles circulating her family details and home address.While considering the petition, the bench directed the police to afford adequate protection to the petitioner’s life as well as her residential apartment. It also directed the police to ensure that the law-and-order situation in the vicinity of the petitioner’s residence is maintained without any sort of obstruction or interference from any person, pending disposal of the petition. The court further sought instructions from the state govt and the police on the petition and adjourned the matter to Oct 26.
Article Summary: Aparna Kurup is coordinating editor of Big TV, a Malayalam news channel. Kurup alleged in her petition that she had faced severe cyberbullying and threats following a programme aired on the channel criticising the remarks made by Samastha Kerala Jamiyyathul Ulama (A P faction)

Article Title: Plea for disqualification: Kerala HC issues notice to EC, MLA Mani C Kappan
Article Text:
MLA Mani C Kappan

Kochi:





The high court on Monday issued notice to the Election Commission and Mani C Kappan, MLA in a petition filed by Dinesh Menon of Mumbai seeking to disqualify Kappan from continuing as an MLA from the Pala constituency following his conviction and sentence to three-and-a-half years’ imprisonment in four cheque cases.A bench of Justice Bechu Kurian Thomas further sought instructions from the Speaker of the state assembly and the state govt, and adjourned the petition to Sept 22 for a detailed hearing. According to Menon, the additional metropolitan magistrate court, Borivali, Mumbai, had convicted and sentenced Kappan to three-and-a-half years’ imprisonment in four cheque cases involving Rs 3.25 crore, filed by Menon on Sept 1. Later, on Sept 9, Menon emailed a representation to the Speaker informing him of Kappan’s conviction and seeking to have him declared disqualified from continuing as a member of the legislative assembly. However, the Speaker’s private secretary informed him that the Speaker would return to Thiruvananthapuram only on Sept 28, prompting him to approach the HC seeking Kappan’s disqualification on account of his conviction and sentence.
Article Summary: Mani C Kappan was convicted and sentenced to three-and-a-half years’ imprisonment in four cheque cases involving Rs 3.25 crore. A bench of Justice Bechu Kurian Thomas further sought instructions from the Speaker of the state assembly and the state govt, and adjourned the petition to Sept 22 for a detailed hearing.
